content: To use the vaginal tablet, lie on your back with your knees bent toward your chest. Insert the tablet or applicator into the vagina as far as it can comfortably go. If you experience itching or burning around the external vaginal area (vulva), apply the skin cream to the affected area once or twice daily for no more than seven days. Continue using this medication daily for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days or if your menstrual period begins. Avoid using tampons, douches, spermicides, or other vaginal products while on this medication. Notify your doctor if your condition does not improve after three days or persists beyond seven days. Additionally, inform your doctor if the infection recurs within two months. Common side effects may include vaginal or urethral burning, itching, pain, or lower abdominal cramps. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. For medical advice about side effects, U.S. residents can call their doctor or the FDA, while Canadian residents should contact their doctor or Health Canada. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other azole antifungal agents (e.g., terconazole, fluconazole), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Consult your doctor about whether sexual intercourse is safe while using this product. Note that this medication may weaken rubber products such as latex condoms, diaphragms, or cervical caps, potentially leading to failure and unintended pregnancy. Avoid using these products during treatment. Do not use this medication for self-treatment if you are pregnant. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, and you should follow your doctor’s instructions on how to use the applicator. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone overdoses on this medication and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. To help prevent vaginal yeast infections, thoroughly dry the genital area after showering, bathing, or swimming. Avoid wearing tight jeans, nylon underwear, pantyhose, wet bathing suits, or damp/sweaty exercise clothes for extended periods. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
